In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the energy absorption capacity of a metal foam can be increased significantly by changing the cell topology.
the foam of higher relative density has a better performance in terms of energy absorption, and the foam of lower relative density has higher energy absorption efficiency.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cell size and distribution are the most important factors for the deformation mechanism of the foams and the deformation is dependent on the cell size and the cell distribution.
the energy absorption capacity of the foam depends on the cell size, cell distribution, and relative density of the foam.
the cell shape and cell size have a significant effect on the energy absorption capacity of aluminium foams.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cell size and cell topology are two key parameters that affect the mechanical behaviour and energy absorption of the foams.
the cell size is not the only parameter that determines the mechanical response of a foam.
the energy absorption capacity of the foam is strongly influenced by cell size, shape and relative density.
